newsitem.title: UK: Monthly Review - Big refugee exodus from Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Monthly Review - Big refugee exodus from Zaire.

text.p: Hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees returned home from camps in eastern Zaire in November, prompting world leaders to scale down a planned multinational humanitarian force for the region.
U.S. President Bill Clinton beat Republican challenger Bob Dole to win a second term.
The world's worst mid-air collision, involving a Saudi Arabian jumbo jet and a Kazakhstan cargo plane, killed 349 people near New Delhi.
Here is a chronology of the main events of the month:
Nov 2 - In Zaire, just over 100 foreign aid workers used a lull in the fighting for control of Goma to cross the border to the Rwandan town of Gisenyi.
Nov 3 - British Telecom unveiled the largest merger in Britain's corporate history, linking up with MCI Communications, the number two U.S. long-distance phone company.
Nov 5 - Spanish Supreme Court judges voted against questioning former prime minister Felipe Gonzalez about a 1980s "dirty war" on Basque rebels.
Nov 5 - Pakistan Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was sacked by the country's president.
Nov 5 - Russian President Boris Yeltsin underwent seven hours of open heart surgery and resumed presidential duties the next day.
Nov 5 - Democrat Bill Clinton was re-elected U.S. president.
Nov 6 - The Bulgarian electoral commission said opposition candidate Petar Stoyanov won the Nov 3 presidential election run-off with 59.73 percent of the vote.
Nov 6 - China released leading dissident Chen Ziming from prison to allow him to receive medical treatment.
Nov 6 - South Africa announced it had suspended a deal to supply arms to the Rwandan government.
Nov 6 - Croatia became the 40th member of the Council of Europe.
Nov 7 - A Nigerian Boeing 727 airliner carrying 142 people crashed some 40 km (25 miles) from Lagos, killing all on board.
Nov 8 - A 19th century Swedish postage stamp was sold for 2.875 million Swiss francs ($2.26 million), making it the single most valuable postage stamp in the world.
Nov 9 - Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic sacked her military chief General Ratko Mladic, who is wanted for alleged war crimes.
Nov 10 - Thirteen people were killed when a powerful bomb blast ripped through a crowd of mourners at a Moscow cemetery.
Nov 12 - Three hundred and forty-nine people died when a Saudi Arabian jumbo jet and a Kazakhstan cargo plane were involved in a mid-air collision near New Delhi.
Nov 12 - U.N. General Assembly adopted a resolution for the fifth year in a row calling for an end to the 30-year-old U.S. trade embargo against Cuba.
Nov 14 - The star of Italy's assault on graft, former magistrate Antonio Di Pietro, resigned as public works minister after coming under investigation himself.
Nov 15 - Indian left-wing extremists killed 13 policemen and one civilian in a rocket attack on Sirpuru village in southern Andhra Pradesh state.
Nov 15 - Hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutus abandoned the Mugunga refugee camp in Zaire and returned home.
Nov 16 - At least 68 people were killed when an explosion destroyed a building housing Russian military officers in the southern republic of Dagestan.
Nov 17 - The five-day U.N.-sponsored World Food Summit ended with calls to end hunger but with deep differences about how to do it.
Nov 17 - Ion Ilescu was defeated in the Romanian presidential elections; Emil Constantinescu won 54 percent of the vote.
Nov 18 - Russian Mars probe plunged into the sea after failing to break out of the Earth's orbit because of a defective booster rocket.
Nov 18 - Fire broke out on a train carrying trucks through the Channel Tunnel, disrupting rail traffic through the link.
Nov 18 - CIA veteran Harold Nicholson was charged with selling classified information to Russia.
Nov 19 - Cuban President Fidel Castro held an historic private audience with Pope John Paul in the Vatican.
Nov 19 - U.S. vetoed a second term for Boutros Boutros-Ghali as U.N. secretary-general; all other 14 members of the Security Council voted in favour.
Nov 20/21 - Hong Kong's worst fire in a building blazed for over 21 hours before being extinguished. At least 39 people were killed when the shop and office block caught fire.
Nov 22 - Australian court sentenced Port Arthur killer Martin Bryant to life in jail for shooting 35 people at a tourist site in Tasmania last April.
Nov 23 - President Boris Yeltsin ordered Russian troops to leave Chechnya.
Nov 23 - One hundred and twenty-five people were killed when a hijacked Ethiopian Airlines Boeing 767 crashed into the sea off the Comoro Islands.
Nov 24 - European Union finance ministers agreed to bring the Italian lira back into the EU's exchange rate mechanism.
Nov 25 - Asia-Pacific leaders ended a summit in the Philippines with a ringing call to transform the lives of half of humanity by creating the biggest free trade zone on earth.
Nov 25 - Iraq's U.N. Ambassador said Baghdad had agreed to all U.N. conditions that had held up implementation of an "oil-for-food" deal.
Nov 25 - Local Zaireans said Tutsi rebels had massacred more than 300 Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees at a camp 40 km (25 miles) southwest of the regional capital Bukavu on November 17.
Nov 26 - South Korea's parliament ratified the country's membership to the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).
Nov 27 - President Nelson Mandela said South Africa would drop recognition of Taiwan in favour of Beijing by the end of 1997.
Nov 27 - Carl Hunziker, a young American detained in North Korea for three months as a spy, was released.
Nov 27 - Indonesia ordered the release of all 124 supporters of opposition figure Megawati Sukarnoputri, imprisoned since riots in July.
Nov 28 - General Ratko Mladic formally gave up leadership of the Bosnian Serb Army.
Nov 28 - Former South Yemen president Ali Nasser Mohammed returned to Aden for the first time since he was ousted in a bloody 1986 coup.
Nov 28 - Algerians voted overwhelmingly for constitutional changes banning Islamic political parties.

Nov 29 - U.N. war crimes tribunal sentenced a Croat to 10 years in jail after he confessed to taking part in the Bosnian Serb Army massacre of over 1,200 unarmed Moslems at Srebrenica. Drazen Erdemovic, 25, was the first person to be sentenced by an international war crimes tribunal since the Nuremberg and Tokyo trials after World War Two.
Nov 30 - At least 100,000 opposition supporters accusing the government of election fraud marched in Belgrade as part of a campaign to try to oust Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.
Nov 30 - Sierra Leone government and rebels signed a comprehensive peace accord to end nearly six years of civil war.

Notable deaths in November included: former Sri Lankan president Junius Richard Jayewardene (1st); former Moroccan prime minister Maati Bouabid (1); Jean-Bedel Bokassa, former self-styled emperor of the Central African Republic (3); Cardinal Joseph Bernardin, senior U.S. Roman Catholic prelate (14); Alger Hiss, U.S. politician accused of being a communist (15); Abdus Salam, Pakistan's only Nobel prize winner (21); Mohamed Amin, noted news cameraman (23); Robert J. McCloskey, U.S. State Department spokesman during the Vietnam War (27).
